title: 2022 AMC 12A Problem 16
statement: A triangular number is a positive integer that can be expressed in the form \(t_n=1+2+3+\cdots+n,\) for some positive integer \(n.\) The three smallest triangular numbers that are also perfect squares are \(t_1=1=1^2,\) \(t_8=36=6^2,\) and \(t_{49}=1225=35^2.\) What is the sum of the digits of the fourth smallest triangular number that is also a perfect square?

solutions.text:
If \(t_n=y^2,\) then \(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}=y^2,\) or \((2n+1)^2-8y^2=1.\) The positive Pell solutions occur successively by multiplying \((2n+1)+y\sqrt8\) by \(3+\sqrt8.\)

Starting from \((2n+1,y)=(3,1),\) this gives \((17,6),\) \((99,35),\) and then \((577,204).\) Thus the fourth value has \(n=288\) and equals \(204^2=41616.\)

The sum of its digits is \(4+1+6+1+6=18.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Generate successive positive solutions by multiplying \((2n+1)+y\sqrt8\) by \(3+\sqrt8\)
